literal: Match names to realities, choose from the multitude and raise the able; let the court have no grandees who reek of copper, and the age be rid of discourse on the Money God.
idiomatic: Match titles to what men truly are; choose widely and promote talent, until no grandee at court smells of coin and the age has done with talk of the Money God.

literal: In old times Baili Xi served Qin, and his name survives in the Sparrow Register;
idiomatic: Long ago Baili Xi became minister of Qin, and his name still lives in the Sparrow Register;

literal: Xiao He and Zhang Liang aided Pei, and their surnames stand in the River Chart.
idiomatic: Xiao He and Zhang Liang helped found Han at Pei, and their houses are written in the River Chart.

literal: Today's ministers and grandees are likewise heaven's gift; to govern with them, what wish would not be followed?
idiomatic: The high ministers of today are heaven's gift as well; rule beside them, and what desire would go unmet?

literal: One need not kowtow to the Celestial Master to hear the art of tending horses;
idiomatic: You need not kowtow to a Celestial Master before you may hear how to tend horses;

literal: nor crawl on one's knees up a mountain to obtain the way of ordering the self.
idiomatic: nor crawl on your knees up a mountain before you learn how to order your own life.

literal: Only let the emperor's virtue be radiant and unceasing in self-strengthening, reading at the first watch of night and passing memorials through the whole day.
idiomatic: Let the emperor's virtue shine clear and his resolve never slacken—books open at the first watch of night, memorials flowing the whole day through.

literal: Zhou Chang's argument likening the ruler to Jie and Zhou—gladly accept it;
idiomatic: When Zhou Chang compares the throne to Jie and Zhou, welcome the words gladly;

literal: Liu Yi's comparison to Huan and Ling—in the end bear it with forbearance.
idiomatic: when Liu Yi compares you to Huan and Ling, in the end swallow the sting and show forbearance.

literal: Hang high the royal ranks and give them only to the able; let no storehouse clerk be passed over, nor any salt-gatherer or fisherman left unrecorded.
idiomatic: Hang the royal ranks high and grant them only to the capable; leave no clerk of the granaries overlooked, no fisherman or salt-worker unlisted.

literal: Do not let Huan Tan, for rejecting prophecy, stop at county aide;
idiomatic: Do not let a Huan Tan, punished for rejecting prophecy, die a county aide;

literal: nor Zhao Yi, for bearing talent, end as a clerical recorder.
idiomatic: nor a Zhao Yi, rich in talent, end his days as a petty recorder.

literal: Then all under Heaven will turn their hearts, dark and bright will know and respond, the year-spirit will serve Han and the wind-lord attend Zhou, the true man will depart and return, the terrace star split and gather again; the Odes praise many officers, the Changes records a host of dragons—from this, one may be without shame.
idiomatic: Then the realm will give you its heart, spirits dark and bright will answer, omens will align as in Han and Zhou of old, sage and star will return to their courses, the Odes will again praise a multitude of men, the Changes a throng of dragons—and on that score, Your Majesty, you need not blush.

literal: He was again asked about the two teachings, Buddhism and Daoism; Xun replied:
idiomatic: He was questioned next on the two teachings, Buddhism and Daoism. Xun answered:

literal: Your servant has heard that the Way of Heaven and fate-nature are what sages do not speak of, because the principle cuts off involvement and is hard to name; yet in Laozi's discourse on the Way and in Zhuangzi's doctrine of free wandering, if one takes the drift of what was left behind, something may still be sought.
idiomatic: I have heard that the Way of Heaven and the matter of fate are what the sages leave unspoken—the principle lies beyond grasp, hard to put into words. Still, in Laozi's talk of the Way and Zhuangzi's teaching of free wandering, if one reads for the meaning behind the words, something can be found.

literal: As for jade slips and golden books, secret scriptures and hidden records, the marvel of the nine-turn rod three feet long, the wonder of crimson snow and dark frost—when Huainan achieved the Way, dogs barked in the clouds; when Prince Qiao gained immortality, swords flew in the sky—all are tales that lean on emptiness.
idiomatic: But jade slips and golden books, secret canon and hidden lore—the three-foot rod turned nine times, elixirs of crimson snow and dark frost—when the King of Huainan 'attained the Way,' dogs were said to bark in the clouds; when Prince Qiao 'became immortal,' swords were said to fly in the sky. These are stories that lean on thin air.

literal: Talk of sea dates and such—seek it like tying the wind, study it like catching a shadow.
idiomatic: Talk of sea-dates and the like is like trying to tie down the wind, or study it like chasing a shadow.

literal: Yet the lords of Yan and Qi, the First Emperor of Qin and the Han emperors trusted those masters of the methods and hoped to meet the true.
idiomatic: Yet the rulers of Yan and Qi, the First Emperor of Qin, and the Han emperors trusted such masters and hoped to meet the Real.

literal: Xu Fu went away and did not return; Luan Da went and obtained nothing.
idiomatic: Xu Fu sailed away and never came back; Luan Da went forth and brought back nothing.

literal: Still they believed that ascending in the far reflection and clapping hands could be expected soon;
idiomatic: Still they believed that to rise in the far reflection and clap their hands was something they could expect any day;

literal: that sacrificing to ghosts and seeking spirits might perhaps grant no death.
idiomatic: that if they sacrificed to ghosts and besought the spirits, they might somehow escape death.

literal: When the river jewel was returned, it entered the tomb on Mount Li;
idiomatic: When the river jewel was 'returned,' it only entered the tomb on Mount Li;

literal: when the dragon steed arrived, it ended beneath the mound at Maoling.
idiomatic: when the dragon steed 'arrived,' it ended beneath the mound at Maoling.

literal: Then one knows that Liu Xiang's faith in the great treasure left him no surplus of blame;
idiomatic: Then one sees that Liu Xiang, who believed in the great treasure, was left with no surplus of excuse;

literal: and Wang Chong's rejection of the Yellow Emperor was, by comparison, not far off.
idiomatic: and that Wang Chong, who rejected the Yellow Emperor legend, was not so far wrong.

literal: Moreover, in recent generations Buddhism has greatly flourished: scriptures copied in the western lands, images painted in the southern palace.
idiomatic: In later ages, moreover, Buddhism has grown vast—scriptures copied from the western lands, images painted in the southern palace.

literal: The Kunming pool's black earth was taken as ash of the burnt kalpa;
idiomatic: The black earth of the Kunming Pool was taken for the ash of a cosmic burn;

literal: a bright night in spring and autumn was called the day spirits descended.
idiomatic: a night in spring or autumn when the sky stayed bright was called the day the gods came down.

literal: The Dharma-king is free and changes without end, setting the world in a mote of dust and fitting Mount Sumeru in a grain of millet.
idiomatic: The Dharma-king is sovereign and without limit, setting the whole world in a speck of dust and packing Mount Sumeru into a grain of millet.

literal: The principle is in essence empty; these are shown as expedients—yet the deluded, grasping at them, beg to leave the household; the Medicine King burned his body, Bo Lun sprinkled his blood—if they could not do even that, they should at least yield their lives.
idiomatic: The root teaching is emptiness; the rest is skillful means shown to the crowd. Yet the deluded clutch at it and beg to leave the world; the Medicine King burned his body, Bodhidharma shed his blood—if they cannot do even that, they should at least be ready to give their lives.

literal: How much less should they change form and appearance to differ from other men, indulge every whim, and in the end be no different from vulgar folk.
idiomatic: How much less should they change their form and face until they hardly seem human, indulge every appetite, and in the end be no better than the common run.

literal: If the leftover doctrines of the dragon palace and the earlier words of the deer park are tolerated, the wind of the Way falls before us.
idiomatic: If the leftover talk of the dragon palace and the old words of the deer park are indulged, the wind of the true Way will fall before it ever rises.

literal: Your servant ventures to consider that Your Majesty, receiving Heaven's bright mandate, has humbled himself to succor the people; mountain ghosts show their spirit, the sea god leads his office.
idiomatic: I venture to think that Your Majesty, having received Heaven's bright mandate, has humbled himself to rescue the people; mountain ghosts show their power, the sea god does his duty.

literal: The stone swallows of Xiangzhong, when the season's rain bathes them, fly in flocks;
idiomatic: The stone swallows of Xiangzhong, when the timely rain washes them, rise in flocks;

literal: the bronze raven on the terrace, complaining of the harmonious wind, turns its ladle.
idiomatic: the bronze raven on the terrace, feeling the fair wind, turns its ladle.

literal: When Zhou made Luoyang its capital, government still lay at Haojing; when Han made its home at Xianyang, its soul returned to Feng and Pei—the lands of Fen and Jin, where royal traces first began: to speak of touring them is already to weary strategy.
idiomatic: When Zhou built Luoyang, rule still lay at Haojing; when Han dwelt at Xianyang, its soul looked back to Feng and Pei. The lands of Fen and Jin, where the royal trace first began—to speak of touring them is already to tax your strategy.

literal: Yet you still lower your mind to the Literary Garden and weigh the hundred schools, thinking to hold jade at Jasper Pool and to seek pearls at Red Water.
idiomatic: Yet you still bend your mind to the Literary Garden and sift the hundred schools, as though to hold jade at Jasper Pool or seek pearls at Red Water.

literal: Your servant considers that when the Queen Mother offered her ring, it was from feeling Zhou's virtue;
idiomatic: I take it that when the Queen Mother of the West offered her ring, she was answering Zhou's virtue;

literal: when Heaven bestowed the girdle-pendant, it was in true reward for Yu's merit.
idiomatic: when Heaven bestowed the girdle-gem, it was true payment for Yu's service.

literal: The two Bans compiled histories, the two Simas made books—none saw the language of the third age, none heard the doctrine of the one vehicle.
idiomatic: The two Bans wrote history, the two Simas wrote prose—none of them knew the phrasing of the third age, none heard the teaching of the one vehicle.

literal: Imperial music and royal rites still changed with the times;
idiomatic: Imperial music and royal rites still shifted with the times;

literal: why doubt winnowing out the left-hand ways and strange folk?
idiomatic: why should you hesitate to winnow out left-hand ways and strange folk?

literal: He was again asked about whether punishments should be lenient or severe; Xun replied:
idiomatic: He was questioned next on whether punishments should be lenient or severe. Xun answered:

literal: Your servant has heard that when a king establishes a state, punishments assist ritual—as cold and heat assist yin and yang, as mountains and rivers thread through heaven and earth.
idiomatic: I have heard that when a true king founds a state, punishments help ritual along—as cold and heat help yin and yang, as mountains and rivers thread through heaven and earth.

literal: From the late age onward, statutes have gradually multiplied; Qin bamboo could not exhaust what was written, Chu slips could not hold it all.
idiomatic: From the late age on, laws have crept wider; Qin could not write them all on bamboo, Chu could not load them on slips.

literal: The clerks, on this basis, opened two gates; high and low lay in their hearts, cold and heat at their whim.
idiomatic: On that basis the clerks opened two gates—high or low at their whim, harsh or mild as they pleased.

literal: The three codes of the Offices of Zhou they tossed aside like blowing fur;
idiomatic: The three codes of the Zhou Offices they tossed aside like blowing fur;

literal: the nine chapters of Han law they broke as easily as turning the hand.
idiomatic: the nine chapters of Han law they broke as easily as turning the hand over.

literal: Thus the miasma of the Longping prison only faded after wine was granted;
idiomatic: So the foul air of the Longping prison only lifted after wine was granted;

literal: the filial woman of Donghai was only whitened by disaster.
idiomatic: the filial woman of Donghai was only cleared when Heaven sent disaster.

literal: Edicts hung on the wall, yet when there was good no one followed it;
idiomatic: Edicts hung on the wall, yet when they commanded good, no one obeyed;

literal: when the corrupt clerk came to the door, nothing was sought that could not be had.
idiomatic: when a corrupt clerk came to the door, nothing was asked that could not be bought.

literal: All because above, the Way was lost; below, the people saw no virtue.
idiomatic: All because above, the Way was lost; below, the people saw no virtue.

literal: Yet those who debate cling to delusion and do not seek the root.
idiomatic: Yet debaters cling to their delusions and never look for the root.

literal: Zhong Yao and Wang Lang pursued grievance against Zhang Cang; Zu Na and Mei Tao together praised Emperor Wen.
idiomatic: Zhong Yao and Wang Lang nursed old grievance against Zhang Cang; Zu Na and Mei Tao together praised Emperor Wen.

literal: They then said that to raise the dead and still the corpse lay in restoring corporal punishment;
idiomatic: From that they said that to raise the dead and still the corpse meant bringing back corporal punishment;

literal: that to order the state and exalt the realm had nothing to do with the rites of Zhou.
idiomatic: that to order the realm and exalt the state had nothing to do with the Zhou rites.

literal: Your servant ventures to consider that Your Majesty, rising before dawn to sit in court, keeps his mind on government and uses clear punishments to correct the feudal lords and extends grace to cherish the hundred surnames.
idiomatic: I venture to think that Your Majesty, rising before dawn to hold court, keeps his mind on government, uses clear punishments to correct the feudal lords, and extends grace to cherish the hundred surnames.

literal: The yellow banner and purple canopy have already left the southeast;
idiomatic: The yellow banner and purple canopy have already quit the southeast;

literal: the white horse and plain carriage are about to descend on Zhi Road.
idiomatic: the white horse and plain carriage are about to come down Zhi Road.

literal: If you again make the code stern and the text deep, your servant truly does not understand.
idiomatic: If you now make the code stern again and the text deep, I truly do not understand.

literal: Why?
idiomatic: Why?

literal: Men resemble heaven and earth and alike receive yin and yang; at peace they wish to live, when disturbed they plot death.
idiomatic: Men mirror heaven and earth and share in yin and yang; when at peace they wish to live, when harried they plot death.

literal: Therefore the king's governance must first attend to ritual and music; if there are those who do not follow, then the penal writings are used; lenience and severity are both set, water and fire both displayed—never has one relied only on Shang Yang and Han Fei and endured long.
idiomatic: So the king's rule must put ritual and music first; only when some still will not follow does the penal code come out. Leniency and severity stand together, water and fire both in view—never yet has a realm leaned only on Shang Yang and Han Fei and lasted.

literal: In old times Qin returned Shi Hui and Jin's thief came to flee;
idiomatic: Long ago Qin sent back Shi Hui and Jin's thief fled to them;

literal: Shun raised Gao Yao and the unkind put themselves far away.
idiomatic: Shun raised Gao Yao and the unkind kept their distance of themselves.

literal: Only let Zhang Shizhi and Yu Dingguo take turns as judges, Gong Sui and Wen Weng succeed one another as prefects, make the statutes one with the fundamental code, rejoice to hear Ji An's words, weep and break off Lord Shao's sentence.
idiomatic: Only let Zhang Shizhi and Yu Dingguo serve in turn as judges, Gong Sui and Wen Weng follow one another as prefects, knit the statutes to a single code, rejoice to hear Ji An speak, weep and set aside the sentence on Lord Shao.

literal: Then all under Heaven will govern itself, the great Way will walk abroad, suckling beasts will bear their tusks, the dark kite will fold its wings, the Chu king's money vault will need no more sealing, and Han's wronged prisoners will naturally receive justice.
idiomatic: Then the realm will order itself, the great Way will walk abroad, suckling beasts will sheathe their tusks, the dark kite will fold its wings, the Chu king's treasury will need no further seal, and Han's wronged prisoners will naturally find justice.

literal: Those beyond the borders, having received the wind, will admire and be transformed;
idiomatic: Those beyond the borders, having caught the wind, will admire and change;

literal: within the trimmed realm all will tread virtue and sing of benevolence.
idiomatic: within the four seas all will tread in virtue and sing of benevolence.

literal: To be hailed as the age of Cheng and Kang—what difficulty is there?
idiomatic: To be hailed as another age of Cheng and Kang—what could be hard about that?

literal: He was again asked about fortune, misfortune, and retribution; Xun replied:
idiomatic: He was questioned next on fortune, misfortune, and retribution. Xun answered:

literal: Your servant has heard that the five directions are easy to distinguish, yet one still waits for the south-pointing chariot;
idiomatic: I have heard that the five directions are easy to tell apart, yet one still waits for the south-pointing chariot;

literal: a hundred generations may be known, yet one still needs to blow the pitch-pipes.
idiomatic: a hundred generations may be foreknown, yet one still must blow the pitch-pipes.

literal: How much more the secret remoteness of Heaven's Way and the hard-to-trace tracks of the spirit—without communion with them, who can fully comprehend?
idiomatic: How much more the secret remoteness of Heaven's Way and the hard-to-trace tracks of the spirits—without communion, who can grasp them whole?

literal: When the raft reached the River of Heaven, one only saw the Cowherd;
idiomatic: When the raft reached the River of Heaven, one only saw the Cowherd Star;

literal: in a feigned sleep one wandered in the upper mystery and only met the Di Dog.
idiomatic: in a feigned sleep one wandered the upper mystery and only met the Di Dog.

literal: The principle of creation and transformation is already silent and without transmission;
idiomatic: The principle of creation and change is already silent and untransmitted;

literal: the coming of retribution is inherently hard to speak of rashly.
idiomatic: the coming of retribution is, by nature, not something to speak of rashly.

literal: Yet Duke Mu of Qin had the Way and Goumang bestowed auspice;
idiomatic: Yet when Duke Mu of Qin held the Way, Goumang granted good omens;

literal: Duke Guo had a cold virtue and Rusou sent down calamity.
idiomatic: when Duke Guo had a cold virtue, Rusou sent calamity down.

literal: What is lofty above surely has its knowing—one cannot say the spirits are dark and hard to trust.
idiomatic: What is high above surely knows—one cannot say the spirits are dark and untrustworthy.

literal: As for Confucius beset at Chen and Cai, Mencius trapped at Qi and Liang—that was simply not meeting the time; how could it concern the principle of fate-nature?
idiomatic: As for Confucius trapped at Chen and Cai, Mencius hard pressed in Qi and Liang—that was simply not meeting the time; what has that to do with the principle of fate?

literal: Wu Zixu without a lord, Sima Qian attached below—receiving execution and taking disgrace: how can one blame others?
idiomatic: Wu Zixu without a lord, Sima Qian clinging to a low post—taking execution and shame: how can one blame others for that?

literal: As for the music harmonizer who found kinship, the oar-man who gained favor—from this, one should be less surprised.
idiomatic: As for the pitch-pipe officer who found favor, the boatman who gained luck—from that angle, there is less to marvel at.

literal: King Wu's floating pestle was Heaven's punishment;
idiomatic: King Wu's floating pestle was Heaven's punishment;

literal: Bai Qi's slaughter of the surrendered was his own intent.
idiomatic: Bai Qi's slaughter of the surrendered was his own intent.

literal: Thus the seven-hundred-year span was still added to the house of Ji;
idiomatic: Thus the seven-hundred-year span was still added to the house of Ji;

literal: the execution at Duyou still fell on Lord Wu'an.
idiomatic: the execution at Duyou still fell on Lord Wu'an.

literal: In old times Han questioned the upper accounts and went no further than eclipses of the sun;
idiomatic: Long ago Han questioned the upper accounts and went no further than solar eclipses;

literal: Jin tested the cultivated talent and stopped at cold fire.
idiomatic: Jin tested the cultivated talent and stopped at cold fire.

literal: Former worthies and past gentlemen all took this as hard;
idiomatic: Former worthies and past gentlemen all took this as hard;

literal: weighing antiquity against today, your servant sees it as easy.
idiomatic: weighing antiquity against today, I see it as easy.

literal: Yet this humble commoner has overborne your grace; thrice broken, cold glue, twice visiting the Golden Horse Gate.
idiomatic: Yet this humble commoner has overborne your grace—lacquer thrice broken, twice admitted at the Golden Horse Gate.

literal: The king's words were bright and splendid; his thought seemed inspired—yet in matching answers he lost the chart and bows deep in fear.
idiomatic: Your words were bright and splendid; my thought seemed touched by the spirits—yet in answering I missed the mark, and I bow deep in fear.

literal: The Secretariat ranked the candidates and made Xun first of his time.
idiomatic: The Secretariat ranked the candidates and placed Xun first in the land.

literal: In the twelfth month, Prince of Qinghe Yue became Grand Commissioner-in-Chief, led troops south to attack, and Xun followed the army.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month Prince of Qinghe Yue became Grand Commissioner-in-Chief, led troops south on campaign, and Xun went with the army.

literal: The next year, the Manifest Ancestor installed the Marquis of Zhenyin as lord of Liang; Yue made Xun acting director of the Grand Commissioner's office and sent him south as envoy to treat for peace with Xiao Xiu and Hou Zhen.
idiomatic: The next year the Manifest Ancestor set up the Marquis of Zhenyin as lord of Liang. Yue made Xun acting director of the Grand Commissioner's office and sent him south to treat for peace with Xiao Xiu and Hou Zhen.

literal: In five days of going and coming he obtained the reply letters of Xiu and the others; Yue then allied with Xiu on the river.
idiomatic: Within five days going and returning he had the reply letters from Xiu and the others; Yue then allied with Xiu on the river.

literal: When the great army returned to Ye, Xun was again recommended by Director of the Ministry of Justice Cui Ang.
idiomatic: When the great army returned to Ye, Xun was again recommended by Cui Ang, Director of the Ministry of Justice.
